rationale: The name and comment describe cancellation, but there is only one reader, no signal or abort, and only a title assertion.
Completion occurs after the start clock. Assertions require a cached read just before completion+TTL and a fresh observable result exactly at expiry.
The assertion covers microsecond order, but the compound requirement also needs equal timestamps with unequal priorities; no such rows are supplied.
A real cursor is obtained, its anchor is removed through the public API, and exact continuation IDs are checked.
The actual setup, calls, and assertions are delegated to checkReaders; its implementation is absent, so the relevant evidence cannot be inspected.
Twelve tests check empty pages, summaries, and query validation. None creates or reuses a cursor with an equivalent reordered or duplicated status set.
The omitted data module determines whether a before cursor is used and whether rows and expected IDs discriminate nearest-previous canonical ordering.
Both public views are requested before the transport resolves, the full identity matches, and one upstream invocation plus both observable outputs are asserted.
A successful read and ID assertion cannot detect shared nested objects: there is no mutation and no later cached read to observe isolation.
The body has relevant assertions, but whether this test is enabled depends on an omitted module. Under the enabled-source rule its coverage status cannot be determined.
An otherwise valid cursor from the real API has only its version changed, then the public list call must reject with the specified code.
Only a fabricated mocked client is called; the real factory is unused. Mock call expectations never observe an upstream signal or real subscriber handling.
The supplied helper awaits the first failure, repeats the same public read, and checks both the recovered content and a second transport invocation.
The only test is statically skipped. Its body is relevant, but the frozen criterion requires enabled test source; this does not make any claim about execution of other tests.
